# Āsaṅkajātaka (Ja 380)
**ID:** Ja 380
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Āsaṅkajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja380

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Āsaṅkajātaka* (Ja 380) is a Jātaka tale delivered by the Buddha while residing at Jetavana to admonish a monk tempted to backslide due to longing for his former wife [SuttaCentral]. Recounting a previous existence, the story tells of an ascetic (the Bodhisatta) who took in a maiden found within a lotus and named her Āsaṅkā because he had crossed the water in doubt (*āsaṅkā*) regarding what lay inside the flower [Cowell 1897]. A king arrived with a fourfold army seeking to claim her, but the Bodhisatta required him to deduce her name before departing with her [Cowell 1897]. The king deliberated in the Himalayas for a year while his troops and beasts succumbed to predators, disease, and harsh winter conditions [Cowell 1897; SuttaCentral]. When the king finally resolved to leave, Āsaṅkā spoke to him of the celestial *āsāvatī* creeper in the Cittalatā garden of Tāvatiṃsa heaven [Cowell 1897]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*), the maiden is identified as the former wife, the king as the backsliding monk (who attained stream-entry upon hearing the teaching), and the hermit as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1883].
Scenes from the *Āsaṅka Jātaka* were also represented in traditional Buddhist visual culture, including Sri Lankan temple murals alongside tales like the *Mahāsudassana* and *Kusa* Jātakas [Dhammapala et al. 1984].
According to SuttaCentral, passage-level parallels exist in other Jātakas (*Hirijātaka*, Ja 363; *Succajajātaka*, Ja 320), the *Theragāthā* (Thag 3.3, Thag 3.15, and Thag 5.2), and the *Saṃyutta Nikāya* (*Ujjhānasaññisutta*, SN 1.35), with a further reference preserved in the *Upālitthera-apadāna* (Tha-Ap 8) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records Pali-internal alignments with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, with no cross-language matches meeting the detection threshold [DharmaNexus].
